arte.universo: Ptolemaic Egypt around 240 BC: the sunlit Greek-Egyptian city of Alexandria by the sea, with white stone columns, courtyards, a tall stone obelisk and a vertical wooden pole casting a short shadow; a huge ancient library hall with wooden shelves full of papyrus scrolls lit by oil lamps; the southern town of Syene on the Nile with a deep stone well, palm trees and desert; a dusty road along the Nile with a distant camel caravan; and a modern Mexican high-school classroom at night today. No portraits and no recognizable real people: the scholar is never shown, only his objects and places. Anonymous people only from behind or far away. No readable writing, letters or digits anywhere.

escena.accion: In a quiet stone courtyard of ancient Alexandria at noon, the Pasita stands next to a tall vertical wooden pole planted in the ground and looks down at its short dark shadow, which glows with a thin lime-green outline on the pale stone floor
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-middle, seen from behind, small school backpack, looking down at the shadow
escena.objeto: A tall vertical wooden pole and its short shadow on the stone floor, the shadow edge softly glowing lime green
escena.foreground: Edge of a stone step and a clay pot, slightly blurred
escena.midground: The Pasita, the pole and its shadow
escena.background: White Greek columns, palm trees, a glimpse of the sea
escena.iluminacion: Strong high sun, warm golden light, crisp short shadows; the sky above darkened by a deep vignette
escena.emocion: Curiosity: a simple shadow hides a big secret
escena.composicion: Medium-wide shot from behind; the upper 42% is a calm, dark, deep-blue vignetted sky for the title

escena.accion: Inside an enormous ancient library hall, the Pasita walks between tall wooden shelves packed with rolled papyrus scrolls, holding one scroll open with both hands
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, three-quarter view from behind, small backpack, reading an open scroll
escena.objeto: Endless shelves of papyrus scrolls; the open scroll has only faint abstract marks (no readable letters)
escena.foreground: A few scrolls on a wooden table, slightly blurred, an oil lamp
escena.background: Shelves and stone columns fading into darkness, one anonymous figure far away seen from behind
escena.iluminacion: Warm oil-lamp light, shafts of dusty light from high windows, deep shadows above
escena.composicion: Wide shot; the upper 42% is the dark, shadowed ceiling and upper shelves

cuerpo: En Siene, **el sol llegaba al fondo de un pozo**.

escena.accion: In the small desert town of Syene by the Nile at noon, the Pasita leans over the stone rim of a deep old well and looks down: far below, the bright round reflection of the sun shines on the water at the very bottom
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, middle-lower part, leaning over the well rim, amazed, small backpack
escena.objeto: A deep round stone well with a bright circle of sunlight reflected on the water at the bottom
escena.foreground: Weathered stones of the well rim, slightly blurred
escena.background: Mud-brick houses, palm trees, the Nile and desert dunes
escena.iluminacion: Sun straight overhead, almost no shadows, golden light; the upper sky darkened by a deep vignette
escena.composicion: Medium shot from slightly above; the upper 42% is a calm dark vignetted sky

escena.accion: At noon in Alexandria, the Pasita kneels on the stone floor beside a tall stone obelisk and stretches a string from the tip of its shadow, measuring the small angle of the sunlight; a thin lime-green line marks the angle
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-right, kneeling, focused, holding the string, small backpack
escena.objeto: The obelisk's shadow on the pale stone and a taut string forming a small glowing lime-green angle (no numbers)
escena.foreground: A wax tablet and a wooden measuring rod on the floor, slightly blurred, no writing
escena.background: The base of the tall obelisk, white columns, the sea
escena.iluminacion: High sun, warm light, crisp shadows; the upper area darkened by a deep vignette
escena.emocion: Concentration: a tiny angle that matters
escena.composicion: Medium shot; the upper 42% is the dark vignetted sky and the shadowed upper obelisk

escena.accion: On a long dusty road beside the Nile at sunset, the Pasita walks with a walking stick, following the river south; far away a small camel caravan travels the same road
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-left, seen from behind, small backpack, walking stick, determined
escena.objeto: The endless road along the Nile stretching to the horizon
escena.foreground: Dry reeds and stones at the roadside, slightly blurred
escena.background: A distant anonymous camel caravan, palm trees, desert hills, the river shining
escena.iluminacion: Warm low sunset light, long shadows, the sky turning deep blue at the top
escena.composicion: Wide shot; the upper 42% is a calm dark dusk sky

cuerpo: Se le reconoce por usar primero **«geografía»**.
Él calculó **250,000 estadios**: no andaba lejos.

escena.accion: In a modern Mexican high-school classroom at night, the Pasita stands on a desk next to a large school globe and stretches a measuring tape around its equator; a thin lime-green line glows along the tape
escena.protagonista: The Pasita, lower-middle, three-quarter view, small backpack, smiling proudly
escena.objeto: A large classroom globe with a measuring tape around the equator (no readable letters or digits)
escena.foreground: School desks and a notebook, slightly blurred, no writing
escena.background: A dark window with city lights, a blank chalkboard
escena.iluminacion: Cold moonlight and a warm desk lamp, soft lime glow on the tape
escena.emocion: Pride and wonder: the ancient idea still works
escena.composicion: Medium-wide shot; the upper 42% is the dark wall and ceiling of the classroom

post:
Hace más de 2,200 años, alguien midió el tamaño de la Tierra sin salir de Egipto. Con un palo, una sombra y mucha paciencia. 🌍

Eratóstenes dirigía la gran biblioteca de Alejandría. Leyó que en Siene, un día al año a mediodía, el sol caía directo al fondo de un pozo. Ese mismo día, en Alejandría, un palo sí hacía sombra: un ángulo de 7.2°, o sea 1/50 de círculo. Como entre las dos ciudades había unos 5,000 estadios, multiplicó por 50: 250,000 estadios.

Hoy sabemos que la vuelta a la Tierra mide unos 40,000 km. Cuánto se acercó depende de qué estadio usó, pero no andaba lejos. Y se le reconoce como el primero en usar la palabra «geografía».

¿Qué medirías tú sin una regla? 👇
